_doc: PRE-MORTEM RETRO ACCEPTANCE CORPUS — the commits we KNOW tripped a recorded
hazard class, with the classes the instrument must name from the changeset
ALONE. This is the same shape that made the reader-with-no-writer walker real:
a guard is not credible until it is run against the thing it claims to catch.
⭐ THE EXPECTATIONS WERE AUTHORED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN, from the commit
messages and the recorded memory — not read back off the instrument's own
output. Fitting expectations to observed output would make the hit rate a
tautology, which is the exact vacuity class this estate keeps recording.
`expectAbsentPredicates` is the NEGATIVE CONTROL. Without it a predicate that
fired on every changeset would post a perfect hit rate carrying no information.
Each case is replayed with `--sha`, so every artifact (bundle metas, size and
tsc baselines, the mutation manifest) is read at the commit's PARENT — the
world as it was when the author was about to make the mistake. Reading today's
artifacts against a commit from last week would prove nothing.
Run: npm run premortem:retro    (add -- --strict to make a miss exit non-zero)

cases.name: Layering repair: git mv of a bundled input + two new un-baselined source files
groundTruth: GIT-mv'd src/generators/hookThemes.js -> src/domain/hookThemes.js. Zero bytes of
the module changed. It was a build input of aiGroundingBundle, so all five edge
bundles went stale and three freshness tests broke; the artifact half had to land
separately at ed8de5c2. The recorded memory names this exact bite: 'the chair
broke it by reading touching bundled inputs as not covering a pure git mv.'
It ALSO added src/domain/spatial/spatialLedgerAccess.js and
src/domain/worldPulse/negotiationEvaluation.js. f16de756's message is the
receipt for the second class: 'the net was ZERO and the ratchet still caught it
— full-config total was 177 before and 177 after; the per-file zero-ceiling law
for un-baselined files is the only reason it reds.'

cases.name: TCD-1: the pin corpus built through the config slot
groundTruth: Added tests/domain/warSeatBooksFactionAddress.test.js, whose corpus builder
called generateSettlementPipeline({ tier }, seed) — tier in the config slot and
the seed in the importedNeighbour slot. Both spellings were silently ignored;
the corpus was single-tier and unseeded while asserting seed-stable behaviour.
Repaired at 65ed49fd (PIN-1) and now refused at the door by
tests/generators/pipelineSeedSlotContract.test.js.

cases.name: SP-F: a new tests/lint walker lands
groundTruth: Added tests/lint/observedShapeReaders.walker.test.js. Any new tests/ file owes
three things at once: the lighting census counts test files and reds on an
addition, an enumerated invariant owes a mutation-coverage-manifest row, and a
new lint/contract test must be proven non-vacuous.

cases.name: NEGATIVE CONTROL — the honest full rebuild, all five bundles in one run
groundTruth: The artifact half of 67f8a58e: `npm run build:edge-shared` run once, rewriting
all five metas. Only three of the five emitted .js files moved, because the
other two bundles' code was byte-identical — which is exactly why the META set,
not the .js set, is the tell. A partial-rebuild warning here would be a FALSE
POSITIVE, and a noisy advisory instrument gets disabled.
